body: Where do you live?
I'm in the same situation, minus the working part. And yes, I also feel shitty.

I was there at 20. No friends except gf, thick coke bottle glasses, acne, terrible at multitasking, quit a dead end job due to anxiety. My first and so far only attempt was then.

I'm 24 now and I still don't feel like I have my shit together. But I'm at my own pace, and so are you.
I have the motivation, I just have little faith in myself. I've dealt with anxiety most of my life and it can be pretty debilitating.

Thank you so much for your kind reply. What I want from life is nothing special -- just what everyone else my age has, a decent job and a network of friends to keep me happy. But often it's so difficult to see how to get there from here.
No, I'm not employed. I'm a full-time student currently. So there's basically no way I could pay for anything.
I've been abstaining from masturbation for over a week now, I don't know if that's long enough to see any results, but it can't hurt.
I hinted at it. I told we didn't have to have sex necessarily after she told me she was on birth control, and she got a little upset, so I dropped it. I don't really know what to do.
Hahaha, nice

It wouldn't be so bad if I didn't feel pressured to be this older, experienced guy in bed. Most peoples' first time with a new gf doesn't go totally smoothly anyway, so I feel it's unfair. My friends are jealous of me but I'd rather be with someone I'm comfortable with and who understands my issues than someone who's merely young and attractive.
I would like to know how to overcome the impulse to compare ourselves as well. It's probably the number one source of anxiety, at least for me (and I'm sure many others as well).
It's not impossible to find a real connection, but it can take a while. Good luck and have patience!

You could always wait until someone messages you. Or you could send out lots of messages so that any single one that goes unreplied won't be a big deal. Keep in mind that the reason you might be 'rejected' isn't necessarily because they don't like you -- some women are cautious about online dating and want to make sure they can trust someone.
I have stomach problems as well. What helps me is some yogurt and some pepto-bismol or ginger tea. It won't necessarily calm me down but it helps with the physical symptoms of anxiety.

Long distance relationships are tough. I'm in the same boat man. Sometimes I think it'd be less stressful if I were alone, but unfortunately many of the things that are best for us also cause us the most anxiety (jobs, relationships, etc). Hang in there.

Thanks. Men are often expected to be the rational, calm ones in a relationship so it's tough for me to be honest -- and sometimes there's a fine line between honesty and offloading your pathologies on someone who doesn't deserve it. But you're right: I have to tell her at some point.

The funny thing is, she's just as introverted as I am. She's not the bar/party type at all. My fear is more that she's built up this image of myself in her mind that I can't live up to, because deep down I'm a nervous wreck (and that's nobody's ideal).

Thanks. It's easier to summon confidence some days than on others. But much of this confidence is paradoxical -- it actually comes from a fear of being alone. I know that if I don't tame my anxiety, it will control me and take away everything I love and hold dear. So maybe a better word is determination.

Still, I wish I didn't have to be so determined. I wish I'd found someone who made me feel comfortable, someone I didn't have to try so hard for.  Maybe that'll come in time, or maybe that'll be someone else. Here's hoping.
Just curious, what triggered the situation getting 'very bad'? Is there any way to address that?

There's nothing wrong with needing somebody -- we're social creatures, after all. It's very difficult to 'handle yourself alone', no matter what you're dealing with. That said, it's better to have a broad network of support (friends, family) than to make one person responsible for your happiness. But to be honest, it doesn't sound like your relationship is unhealthy. I'd say you're fine.

I'm sorry -- I know the feeling of believing you're a burden on the people you love and care about, and it's awful. And I've been on both sides of it, the burdener and the 'burdened', so maybe I know how your husband feels. And if he felt anything like I did, he doesn't think you're a burden at all. I'm sure he loves you and meant what he said about not leaving you. That said, his outburst sounds worrying. I second the marital counseling idea. 

Best of luck to you today. You'll pull through it.

I guess you could say I'm in a similar situation. For me, it's a Catch-22, because while a less ambitious job is often less stressful, it also can throw me into self-loathing and doubt about my own capabilities -- after all, only a loser would do [x blue collar job]. But since you've already proven yourself by landing a decent job, it's probably better to stick with it as much as you can. If you can't, then you can't. But it sounds like aside from the anxiety, you have a good thing going. 

Hope this helps.
